problems: The right wing root star (30324) sits off the body outline, slightly detached from the torso, so the right wing reads as a separate piece.
The wings are thin, sliver-like outlines, which weakens the silhouette and makes it closer to a cross or moth shape than a gull.
Labels crowd each other: 'tail base' and 'tail tip' nearly overlap, and 'right wing middle' and 'lower right wingtip' sit on the wing outline.
The head is small and the neck is a thin spike, so the head/neck read weakly as body parts.
The blue outline is a traced silhouette around the gold lines, which is acceptable, but the lower body is narrow and the breast/belly stars sit right on the gold spine rather than inside a body mass.
output.advice: Keep the overall pose: head up-right (star 31084 at top), tail down (31125 and 31416 at bottom), wings spread left and right. Widen the body so it becomes a real torso mass around the breast (31700, approx. 243,301), belly (31592, approx. 252,328) and shoulder (32349, approx. 199,264), and move the right wing root (30324, approx. 336,296) into the body edge so the right wing connects to the torso. Thicken the wings toward the middle, from the root to the wingtips (34045 at left, approx. 85,238; 28910 at upper right, approx. 441,222; 28816 at lower right, approx. 447,262), so they read as gull wings and not as a moth. Make the neck (31827) a visible short thick section between the shoulder and head. Nudge the tail labels apart so 'tail base' and 'tail tip' do not overlap, and move the wing-middle label off the outline.
